summary: Split publishing into two tracks built from this one repo: main publishes the open, indexable live site, and staging publishes a permanent passphrase-gated review site at review.harvardintech.com that shows drafts and is the only place /admin is served. Promotion to live becomes a single one-click workflow instead of a git exercise.

changes.title: The preview gate became an explicit switch
changes.description: PREVIEW_GATE_ENABLED used to be Boolean(process.env.DEPLOY_BASE_PATH) — the deploy's base-path variable. That coupling made two simultaneous tracks impossible, because the site was either a gated project-site preview or a public custom-domain launch, never both. It also meant the eventual domain cutover would silently un-gate the preview as a side effect, which is not a decision a base path should be making. The gate now reads its own PREVIEW_GATE variable, set per track by the deploy workflow, and the shared envFlagEnabled rule decides what counts as on. That rule is deliberately strict — only the exact string '1' — so a typo like PREVIEW_GATE: 'ture' leaves a build gated-off and public rather than having its intent guessed at. astro dev still leaves the gate off, so scenario captures are never overlaid by the passphrase prompt.

changes.title: Draft visibility is now per-track, not per-environment
changes.description: Every publishedEntries call site used to inline !import.meta.env.PROD, so any deployed build hid drafts exactly like production did. That inference cannot express the review track, because the review site IS a production build that must show drafts. A shared INCLUDE_DRAFTS flag replaces it across all nine call sites — the homepage, the site-wide nav in BaseLayout, and the events, donate, volunteer, sponsor, blog, chapters and communities routes. Drafts now appear under astro dev and on the review track, and never on the public build. publishedEntries itself is untouched: it already took includeDrafts as a parameter for exactly this reason, so only its arguments changed.

waysToTest.text: Read src/lib/draftVisibility.test.ts — the case that matters is 'shows drafts on a production build that opts in', which is the review track and the thing the old inference could not express.
Verified end to end against real builds: a post with draft: true got no route and was absent from the blog index and homepage in the public build, and was routed and listed in the review build.

tests.description: astro dev, and therefore the codeyam preview and every scenario capture — an author sees the entry they are writing without setting anything.

changes.title: The CMS admin and the sitemap ship only where they belong
changes.description: /admin is now built only on the gated review origin and under astro dev, never on the public site. This is the change that makes draft-phasing mean anything: the admin pages embed each entry's raw markdown directly in their static HTML, and the CMS sign-in gate is client-side only, so wherever /admin deploys, every draft's full source is publicly fetchable. Keeping it on the passphrase-gated origin is what stops that being a public leak. The sitemap moved the opposite way — public track only, since a noindex origin serving Disallow has nothing to offer one. Both decisions were lifted out of astro.config.mjs into a small module so they could be unit-tested; the config file itself can only be exercised by a real astro build and cannot be imported under vitest.

changes.title: robots.txt tells the truth on both tracks
changes.description: The robots endpoint already switched between Allow and Disallow off the gate, but it emitted its Sitemap line unconditionally — so once the sitemap integration was removed from the review track, the review site would have pointed crawlers at a sitemap-index.xml that 404s. That was a real bug introduced by the track split and caught by building the review site for real. The policy body was pulled out of the endpoint into a pure function taking the gate as a parameter, which is what makes both tracks testable at all: the endpoint resolves the gate from process.env at module load, so a test importing it could only ever reach the public branch. The endpoint keeps origin resolution and response shaping.

waysToTest.text: Read src/lib/robots.test.ts — 'omits the Sitemap line entirely when gated' is the regression guard for the bug this change fixes.
Verified against real builds: the public robots.txt carries Allow plus a Sitemap line; the review robots.txt is Disallow with no Sitemap line at all.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody review track › omits the Sitemap line entirely when gated
tests.description: The bug this extraction exists to pin — the review track has no sitemap, so advertising one would send crawlers to a 404.

example.note: The sitemap URL is passed in and deliberately unused — the gated track has no sitemap to advertise.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody review track › disallows all crawlers when gated
tests.description: The gated review origin must tell crawlers to stay out entirely.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody public track › allows all crawlers when not disallowing
tests.description: The open, indexable site invites every crawler.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody public track › points the Sitemap at the url it was given
tests.description: The Sitemap line carries the caller's resolved origin, not a placeholder — the regression the original static robots.txt shipped.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody formatting › puts the directive on its own line under the user-agent
tests.description: Crawlers parse line-by-line, so the directive must not be concatenated onto the user-agent line.

tests.name: robotsTxtBody formatting › ends with a newline on both tracks
tests.description: A trailing newline keeps the last directive well-formed for line-based parsers.

changes.title: Two deploy tracks and a one-click promote
changes.description: The deploy workflow now triggers on both main and staging and builds whichever track was pushed, replacing the single withastro/action step with explicit setup-node, npm ci and npm run build so each track gets its own environment. The public track publishes through the existing Pages artifact pair; the review track writes a CNAME and .nojekyll and pushes its output to a second repo over an SSH deploy key, because one GitHub repo hosts exactly one Pages site. A new promote workflow fast-forwards staging into main from the Actions tab — and opens a pull request instead if main has diverged, rather than attempting an unattended merge. It then invokes the deploy workflow directly, because a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN does not itself trigger one. The CMS was pointed at staging so every editor commit lands on the review track first.

waysToTest.text: CI workflows cannot be exercised locally. Both files were parsed to confirm valid YAML and job structure, and the builds they invoke were run directly with each track's environment. The review track cannot actually publish until the one-time manual setup in DEPLOY_SETUP.md is done — until then a push to staging fails at its publish step and the public track is unaffected.

The build-time behavior these workflows select is covered by src/lib/publishTrack.test.ts, src/lib/draftVisibility.test.ts and src/lib/envFlag.test.ts — the workflows only set the environment those read.

changes.title: Docs describe the two-track model
changes.description: CMS_SETUP.md gained a section on where edits land and how to promote, written for content editors rather than engineers, plus a table separating the two things that phase a change: the per-entry Draft toggle phases content, the staging branch phases everything. DEPLOY_SETUP.md gained the per-track table, the environment-variable matrix, and a numbered one-time setup checklist for the review repo, deploy key, staging branch, Pages configuration and DNS record — including an honest note that the passphrase is a deterrent rather than authentication, and what to switch to if that is not enough. The scoping README's open preview-access decision is marked resolved, the review handoff links now point at the review domain, and the domain-transfer runbook notes that the cutover no longer un-gates anything.

waysToTest.text: Prose. Read DEPLOY_SETUP.md's review-track setup section — it is the checklist that has to be worked through before review.harvardintech.com exists.
